Definition: caprice (as a fit coming on), i.e. vexation; concretely a tyrant
BiblicalUsage: Isaiah says God will give children to be the princes of a rebellious people, and their rulers will be babes; their oppressors will be caprice itself. Then he says God will choose their delusions, and bring their fears upon them, because when He called, none answered. The word is wantonness, caprice, a fit of vexation: rule by whim instead of wisdom.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Isaiah's warning is plain: a people that will not listen to God will end up ruled by whims, their own and their rulers', and God lets them have what they chose.
